column1: # check-surface-discovery.tsv — the DISPOSITION LEDGER that turns the
# degenerate-input registry from a seed into a CLASS (temperloop#1491,
# follow-up to temperloop#1476, epic #1409).
# WHAT PROBLEM THIS FILE SOLVES. check-surface-registry.tsv is opt-in: a
# check surface nobody registered was not failed, it was simply not checked.
# So the registry documented what somebody REMEMBERED, and a check surface
# added next month inherited the exact defect epic #1409 exists to close,
# silently. The fix is not a longer registry (a longer list is still a list
# somebody sampled) — it is the §5 DISCOVERY PASS in
# validate-check-surface-degenerate-coverage.sh, which enumerates the
# candidate set MECHANICALLY from the tree and FAILS on any candidate that
# has no disposition anywhere. This file is where a candidate that is
# deliberately NOT registered records WHY. Silence stopped being a legal
# answer; an explicit, reviewed reason is now the only way out.
# THE DISCOVERY PREDICATE (owned by the gate's §5 — restated here for the
# reader, not duplicated as logic): every tracked file under the repo root
# whose basename matches `validate-*.sh`, `check-*.sh`, or `lint-*.sh`, with
# `tests/`, `fixtures/`, `node_modules/` and `.git/` pruned, plus the
# vendored `kernel/` subtree pruned in a composed overlay (its rows are
# upstream-owned and upstream-checked).
# WHAT THE PREDICATE CANNOT SEE — stated, not implied. Two candidate classes
# are out of its reach BY CONSTRUCTION, and both keep their existing home:
#   1. SUBCOMMAND surfaces (`replay.sh:diff-scope`) — no filename glob can
#      find a check-shaped subcommand of a general orchestration script.
#      That is exactly why the registry is a registry and not a glob, and
#      those surfaces are registered/allowlisted by hand as before.
#   2. Check-shaped scripts OUTSIDE the three name families — a hook
#      (`claude/hooks/*-guard.sh`), a Makefile recipe body. Hooks are a
#      deliberately different contract: they FAIL OPEN by design (a guard
#      that cannot evaluate must not block the operator), which is the exact
#      inverse of this class's fail-closed rule, so folding them in would
#      register a contradiction.
# Widening the predicate to a fourth name family is a one-line change in the
# gate; widening it to the two classes above is a design question, not an
# omission.
# FORMAT — TAB-separated, exactly three columns:
#   1. SURFACE      same grammar as check-surface-registry.tsv's SURFACE
#                   column (a script path, or `<script-path>:<subcommand>`)
#   2. DISPOSITION  pending | excluded
#                     pending   a genuine check surface that SHOULD be
#                               registered and is not yet. SHRINK-ONLY (see
#                               below): a `pending` row may be removed (the
#                               surface got registered) but never ADDED.
#                     excluded  a discovered path that is deliberately not a
#                               registrable check surface at all. Growable,
#                               because a newly-added script legitimately
#                               matching the name glob but not being a gated
#                               check needs a home — but every `excluded`
#                               row is a reviewed claim in the diff, exactly
#                               like the registry's own `not-applicable`.
#   3. REASON       mandatory, non-empty, one line. For `pending`, say what
#                   BLOCKS registration (and name the tracking issue when one
#                   exists); for `excluded`, say why it is not a check
#                   surface this class governs.
# THE PENDING RATCHET (§4c of the gate). The `pending` set may only SHRINK
# relative to the ratchet base ref, exactly like
# check-surface-degenerate-allowlist.tsv. Without that, this file would be a
# nicer-looking version of the hole it closes: a new unregistered surface
# could be parked here forever with a one-line excuse. It cannot — a NEW
# check surface must be registered, or argued as `excluded` in review.
# ADOPTION NOTE FOR A CONSUMING REPO. An ABSENT ledger means ZERO
# dispositions, so the discovery pass requires every discovered surface to be
# registered or allowlisted — fail-closed, deliberately, and consistent with
# how this gate already treats its other inputs. A repo adopting the kernel
# creates this file and dispositions its own surfaces; the gate's failure
# output names every one of them, so the list is mechanical, not archaeology.
# ── pending: no input-path fixture seam ────────────────────────────────────
# These surfaces derive their scan set from their own location (a fixed
# repo-relative path or `git ls-files`) and read NO environment override, so
# no absent/unreadable/empty input can be injected without first adding a
# scan-root seam. That seam is the prerequisite work, not a fixture — which
# is why they are `pending` rather than registered with a fabricated
# `not-applicable` claim.
